facts.text: I keep getting bouts of fever that come and go.
I get a red rash that is tender to the touch.
It's mostly on my trunk.

facts.item: how long the flares have been going on
aliases: how long the symptoms have been going on
facts.text: This has been happening for about 2 years.
Each flare lasts 3 to 7 days.
They come back about every 3 weeks.
Some flares are bad enough that I'm stuck in bed.

aliases: feeling like I have the flu
facts.text: Before a flare starts, I feel like I'm coming down with the flu.
Before a flare I already run a low-grade fever.
Before a flare I get a sore throat.
Before a flare my joints ache.
During the flares I get diarrhea on and off.
During the flares I get severe headaches.
I get seasonal hay fever.
Apart from my seasonal hay fever, I don't have any medical problems.
No one in my family has an autoimmune disease.
I've tried several different antihistamines.
They didn't help.
I've taken prednisone tablets.
It didn't help.
I've had monthly omalizumab injections.
They didn't help.
I'm White.

findings.name: skin biopsy of the rash
findings.result: Perivascular neutrophilic infiltrate without evidence of leukocytoclastic vasculitis.

findings.name: complement levels
findings.result: C4 mildly decreased (12.8 mg/mL); C3 normal.

findings.name: autoimmune serology
findings.result: Antinuclear antibodies negative; antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies negative; rheumatoid factor negative.

findings.name: viral serology
findings.result: Hepatitis screening negative; HIV screening negative.

findings.name: colonoscopy
findings.result: No evidence of inflammatory bowel disease.

gold.reasoning: 1. Urticarial vasculitis considered and excluded — “demonstrated perivascular neutrophilic infiltrate with no evidence of leukocytoclastic vasculitis.” 2. Chronic spontaneous urticaria considered and excluded — “The chronic urticaria index was within normal limits.” and “patient trialed multiple antihistamines … and monthly omalizumab … with no relief.” 3. Crohn’s disease considered and excluded — “A colonoscopy was performed with no evidence of inflammatory bowel disease.” 4. Blau syndrome considered and excluded — “BS is primarily a pediatric disease characterized by a triad of granulomatous dermatitis, uveitis, and inflammatory arthritis. Development of disease in adults and the presence of fever, abdominal pain, and diarrhea are rarely seen.”

source_issues: C4 is given as 12.8 mg/mL; serum C4 is normally reported in mg/dL, so the unit is probably a typo. Kept as written.
s007 runs several tests into one list ('normal thyroid hormones, C-reactive protein, erythrocyte sedimentation rate'); CRP and ESR are read as normal.
notes: Index visit: the outpatient presentation after 2 years of recurrent flares of fever and tender rash (s001-s004, s006); the rash biopsy, laboratory tests and colonoscopy (s005, s007, s008) are findings of the same staged workup.
The source does not say when the rash biopsy, the laboratory tests and the colonoscopy were done relative to the index visit, so these findings carry no time.
Flare-wide attributes (2-year duration, 3-7 days per flare, every 3 weeks, sometimes bedbound) are standalone facts with general items because they describe the whole episode, not one symptom.
Earlier treatments (antihistamines, prednisone, omalizumab) are medication facts with a treatment_response child each, because the patient took them before the index visit.
s008: the clause 'Because of his gastrointestinal symptoms' is the clinician's reason for the colonoscopy, not a finding; the colonoscopy result is kept.
